Conjunction details: object 58321 fragmentation debris, closest approach T+120 min, predicted miss 180 m, Pc 2.1e-4 > threshold 1e-4. Avoidance chain mentions avoidance burn uses 1 N thrusters (P-PROP-04). Each needs its catalyst bed preheated to 315°C (P-PROP-05, REQ-PROP-028) before firing, so burn timing depends on that heater.

e.markdown:
**Diagnosis**
At T+2 min telemetry TM-CONJ-02 shows a collision probability of 0.00021 (Pc = 2.1×10⁻⁴) for CDM-0412, exceeding the 1×10⁻⁴ action threshold, with a predicted miss distance of 180 m and closest approach at T+120 min. The avoidance chain states that a burn using the 1 N thruster P-PROP-04 is required, and that the thruster’s catalyst bed (P-PROP-05) must be preheated to 315 °C per REQ-PROP-028 before firing. The build record NCR-002 reveals that the heater element measures 52 Ω against the 46 ± 2 Ω drawing limit, so the bed reaches only 290 °C after 30 min at 12 W; the MRB accepted it “Use-as-is under deviation” with the basis that thrusters still reach 315 °C but only slower, about 43.4 min instead of 30 min. Consequently every burn needs roughly 13 min more preheat than the spec allows (flight impact statement in NCR-002).

**Why the build record mattered**
The spec-sheet model assumes a 30 min preheat, yielding a decision deadline of T+45 min (spec model in the autonomy policy counterfactual). NCR-002 shows the actual preheat time is 43.4 min, moving the required preheat start to T+32 min to finish before the burn must occur. Without accounting for this slower heater, the burn would miss the window; with the as-built preheat time, the policy correctly set the deadline to T+32 min, before the next operator contact at T+38 min, and authorised an autonomous preheat-then-burn sequence.

**For the operator**

*At the next pass (Svalbard, T+38 min)*
- Verify that preheat of P-PROP-05 began no later than T+32 min and check temperature telemetry (if available) to confirm the bed has reached ≥315 °C.
- Confirm that the collision-avoidance burn command was uplinked and that the burn initiated at the planned time (~T+45 min) via thruster status or delta-v telemetry.
- Check post-burn orbit parameters (e.g., along-track delta-v) against the predicted 0.075 m/s to ensure the maneuver executed.

*Afterwards*
- Around T+45 min (after burn completion), monitor TM-CONJ-02 or the navigation solution to verify the miss distance has increased and Pc has fallen below the 1×10⁻⁴ threshold.
- At the next operator contact (McMurdo, T+133 min), perform a health check of P-PROP-04 and P-PROP-05 (heater current, thruster valve pressure) to detect any burn-related degradation.
- Log the observed preheat duration for future planning; any discrepancy from the nominal 30 min assumption will be addressed in the next build via an NCR.
